text: {"side":"artifact","claims":[{"text":"Blend contamination is the leading non-astrophysical explanation: 350 of 564 trigger points (about 62%) are flagged BLEND_SUSPECT, so a neighbouring star could be contaminating the photometry at many epochs.","evidence_ids":["E-058"]},{"text":"Several listed detections carry a BLEND_SUSPECT tag together with a SHAPE_OUTLIER tag, including the deep negative dips on rh07064e0s0 and rh08003e0s0, which fits a blended or distorted image rather than a real brightening or dimming.","evidence_ids":["E-047","E-049","E-051","E-053"]},{"text":"Plate-edge and emulsion defects are present in the trigger: 35 points are flagged PLATE_EDGE and 35 flagged as non-blue emulsion, and a listed point on md27229e0s0 is both a plate-edge hit and a 0.39 mag offset, so edge or emulsion effects could mimic part of the signal.","evidence_ids":["E-061","E-056","E-044","E-048"]},{"text":"The candidate spans 1920 to 1952 and its listed offsets straddle plate-series boundaries (for example mc, ma, i, rh, and rl series with differing zero points from -0.194 to +0.573), so a series-zero-point or seam offset could produce an apparent step; the series zero points differ by more than 0.5 mag across series.","evidence_ids":["E-002","E-033","E-038","E-039","E-015"]},{"text":"The known-variable and plate-offset checks pass, and the event's amplitude is not a lower limit, but these checks do not clear the blend, shape, and edge flags, and only 30 of 564 points are shown, so the evidence cannot rule out an artifact and the case that the event is an artifact remains unconfirmed.","evidence_ids":["E-067","E-064","E-055","E-003"]}]}
